key_insight: SteelAgent’s apparent accuracy and uncertainty reliability depend strongly on whether evaluation holds out random samples, steel families, or data sources.
engineering_relevance: Steel property estimates used for alloy selection or compliance decisions should state the evaluation population and uncertainty performance on relevant held-out groups.
method: Combine metallurgical descriptors and machine-learning models with an LLM interface for prediction, uncertainty reporting, and inverse design.
Audit generalization using random splits and held-out steel families, sources, and laboratory grades.
Compare physics-derived features and examine group-level errors and calibration.
evidence_signal: On SteelBench tensile-strength evaluations, gradient-boosting pooled out-of-fold R² fell from 0.859 with random splitting to 0.113 with family holdout; nominal 90% interval coverage was 91.0% under random splitting versus 37.6% on held-out sources.
watch_item: Physics-derived features were not consistently beneficial: gradient-boosting R² increased by 0.2534 in a 17-family holdout analysis but decreased by 0.358 in a separate four-grade laboratory analysis.
paper_title: SteelAgent: LLM-Orchestrated, Physics-Informed Steel Property Prediction with Audited Generalization and Calibrated Uncertainty
